decisions.reason: Despite no longer being observed on the website, the adjustable cardboard quarter-pallet display remains very close to the firm's core POS display competence and is still worth retaining as a standard solution.
The pegboard-back cardboard display is a useful variant within the firm's established retail display range and supports customer-specific merchandising needs without stretching capabilities.

This standard cardboard quarter-pallet display overlaps with other formats and is therefore more exposed to rationalisation, but it still fits the firm's focused display portfolio well enough to keep for now.
The eighth-pallet format helps serve smaller retail footprints and remains a sensible extension of the firm's established cardboard display offer.

The wooden display pallet is less central to a paper-based display specialist and, after disappearing from view, is the clearest candidate to discontinue and free resources for core cardboard solutions.

This media-oriented quarter-pallet display is more niche and more overlapping with the firm's other cardboard pallet variants, making it a likely product to withdraw in favour of broader core formats.
